_comment: systems/realmDecline.js — the weight of greatness. Four strains (0-100) on a realm the player rules creep toward a pressure set by its size, its age and the House's years on the throne; countermeasures knock them down and they creep back over years. 'bite' = (strain - biteFrom) / (100 - biteFrom), 0..1: every effect scales with it. Weekly ticks (cadence days); a year is 120 days.
_rise: share of the gap to the pressure closed each week while the strain is below it (0.006: about ten years to close two thirds of the gap); fall: the same, when the pressure has dropped below the strain

graft.label: Court bloat and graft
graft.blurb: Clerks multiply, offices are farmed out, and the treasury leaks into the purses of the men who keep it.

drift.label: Far provinces drifting
drift.blurb: The farther a town lies from the crown, the more its lord acts as his own king: dues kept back, the king's writ obeyed when it suits.

soft.label: Heirs born in the purple
soft.blurb: Children raised among silk and flatterers come of age soft: fearful, greedy, fond of the cup.

entrench.label: Guilds and clergy entrenched
entrench.blurb: Old charters, old benefices: the guild halls and the cathedral chapters have their privileges in writing and will not be moved.

audit.label: Audit the treasury
audit.blurb: Royal auditors go through every ledger. A share of what was skimmed comes back; those who skimmed it will not forget.

reorganise.label: Reorganise the provinces
reorganise.blurb: New shires, new sheriffs, the king's judges riding circuit in the far towns. Dear, and the far lords lose their little kingdoms.

purge.label: Purge the court
purge.blurb: Arrest the worst of them, seize their purses, strip the guilds and chapters of their charters. Every lord in the realm takes note — and some will rise.

moveCapital.label: Move the capital
moveCapital.blurb: Leave the old court and its parasites behind: raise a new seat nearer the heart of the realm.

marchCommand.label: Give an heir a march command
marchCommand.blurb: Send a grown child to hold a far border for two years, among soldiers and hard winters. They come home harder — and sometimes scarred.

bite.graft: The court of {realm} has grown fat: clerks on clerks, and the treasury leaks {pct}% of its dues into their purses.
bite.drift: The far towns of {realm} drift from the crown; their lords keep their own counsel and a part of the king's dues.
bite.soft: The children of the court of {realm} grow up soft. Heirs raised at home will come of age weaker for it.
bite.entrench: The guilds and the chapters of {realm} have dug in: every edict costs more to proclaim and keep.

grave.graft: Graft eats the treasury of {realm}. Unless the books are audited or the court purged, the crown pays a fortune to its own servants.
grave.drift: The far provinces of {realm} are crowns in all but name. Reorganise them, or move the capital nearer, before they go their own way.
grave.soft: No heir raised at the court of {realm} comes of age hard. Send them away — to the marches, to another court, to the church.
grave.entrench: The old charters of {realm} bind the crown hand and foot. A purge, or a new capital, would break them.
